newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INDIA SEALS KPC TERM DIESEL, KERO AT LOWER PRICES.
newsitem.headline: INDIA SEALS KPC TERM DIESEL, KERO AT LOWER PRICES.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has renewed its term purchase contract of high speed diesel and superior kerosene from Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) for April 1997-March 1998 at lower prices than in the previous year, industry sources said on Friday.
IOC raised its purchase of 1.0 percent sulphur diesel to 2.07 million barrels from 1.5 million barrels, at a premium of 25 cents per barrel to MidEast spot quotes, on a free-on-board (fob) basis.
The price for the previous contract was a 70-cent premium to MidEast spot quotes, fob basis.

IOC paid a premium of 92 cents per barrel to MidEast spot quotes for 1.08 million barrels of 0.25 percent sulphur diesel, fob basis. This marks the start of a formal contract for the 0.25-percent grade with KPC, source said.
Previously, India bought on an adhoc basis two-45,000-tonne cargoes a month of this grade at a $1.25-premium, fob basis, from last December.
